reviewSummary.decision: All native candidates preserve count-level anatomy but fail the user-visible dinosaur-motion amplitude gate. Retain the cleanest full-range v1 and deterministic nostril-dust derivative as internal audit evidence only; do not publish either under the 2026-08-07 subject-motion policy.

policy.scope: ComfyUI-native Wan2.2 TI2V 5B forward-only solo dinosaur action candidate for a children's dinosaur atlas
policy.publicationRule: Publish only after readable dinosaur subject motion plus all-frame anatomy and temporal review. Reject fixed-dinosaur environment-only fallbacks, horn-count drift, frill melting, neck separation, body or foot sliding, reverse motion, return motion, repeated motion, or any unsafe prefix. If no clean subject-moving forward segment exists, omit the public sample and retain audit evidence internally.

candidates.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame Triceratops horridus identity, anatomy, left-facing profile, full-body composition, forest, ground, lighting, palette, skin pattern, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Triceratops remains planted in the source coordinates, with one solid skull-attached frill, exactly two long brow horns, exactly one shorter nasal horn, one closed hooked beak, exactly two forelimbs, exactly two hind limbs and four stable weight-bearing feet, and one complete continuous tail. After a brief still opening, the animal performs one calm continuous head lift only: the complete skull, all three horns, solid frill, short neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest rise together by only three to four degrees in one forward direction, with no hinge, gap, stretching, or isolated frill rotation. The motion starts slowly, continues smoothly, and ends in the slightly higher attentive pose for the final second. The beak stays closed. Horn count, horn length, frill outline, neck thickness, eye position, and skin markings stay constant. The torso, pelvis, complete tail, all four planted feet, every readable toe, and the background remain fixed at their source coordinates. No return movement, no reverse, no second nod, no looping, no walking, no roar. Keep anatomy crisp, camera fixed, exposure stable, and the final frame a natural continuation rather than a duplicate of the first frame.

candidates.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. One fixed wide camera and one continuous five-second forward-only shot. Preserve the approved first frame and exactly one complete Triceratops horridus with one solid attached frill, two long brow horns, one shorter nasal horn, a closed beak, four planted legs and feet, and one complete tail. Make one clear alert head raise that is easy to see: the animal begins with its head low, then steadily raises the entire skull, all three horns, frill, short muscular neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest together by twelve to fifteen degrees. This is one smooth rising arc across the whole clip. The final head and horn tips are visibly higher than at the start and remain at the high pose; there is no return and no second nod. Keep the frill rigidly attached to the skull and distribute the lift through the broad neck root into the shoulders. Preserve horn count, horn length, frill edge, neck thickness, closed beak, eye, skin markings, torso, tail, four feet, ground contact, background, camera, exposure, and crop. The torso does not walk or translate. No reverse, loop, roar, cut, pan, zoom, or background motion.
